- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.

Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

I need to make a Monopoly decision.

I'm on the Jail space as a visitor. All my properties are mortgaged. p2 has a massive empire and $211 cash. p1 and p4 are bankrupt. The bank has 5 houses and 10 hotels left.

Unmortgaging would burn my $203 cash buffer without stopping p2. Virginia is the worst choice because it completes p2's pink set. I will end the turn.

Rolling from Jail next turn could hit p2's utilities, St. James with three houses, or the orange set. I am calculating exact rent values for those spaces.

Three houses on p2's orange set would cost $550 to $750. That exceeds my $203 cash. I would go bankrupt on rolls 7 through 9. Rolling 6 lands on the Pennsylvania RR for $200. I would survive with $3 left. Rolls 10 through 12 are safe.

The electric company costs $30 on a roll of 3. St. Charles and States each cost $10 because Virginia is mortgaged and blocks the pink monopoly. The danger from Jail is 15 of 36 rolls.

Unmortgaging any property would reduce my cash below $200. That would make the $200 railroad rent from Jail bankrupt me. I will end the turn.
